title: inference-call-comprehensive-task-ticket
owner: CC owns the mechanism. Akien owns the field list (what gets recorded) and the trouble integration design.
intention: Every inference call produces a comprehensive task ticket recording the full lifecycle: who asked (call chain or message envelope), request, answer, model/provider selection, escalations, exceptions, graph tree nodes consulted, and outcome — so the call can be learned from or debugged after the fact.
why: Akien, 2026-08-18: 'a task ticket is created with all the information. who asked, what the request was, what the answer was, model specified if any, model selected, provider specified if any, provider selected, escalations along the way and their back and forth, exceptions thrown... everything we might need in order to learn from the call, or to debug a failure later.' The existing interceptor records calls but not the full lifecycle — caller identity, selection rationale, escalation history, and trouble integration are missing.
traces_to: Law 7 — the task ticket is the record of truth for what happened during the call; errors are loud and permanent.
Law 10 — every recorded observation is measurement; the task ticket records every observable aspect of the call.
Law 1 — the task ticket is the settled answer to 'what happened', preventing re-derivation.

falsifier.proves_green: code-seam invariant: proved + feeds-back-on-failure. PROVE GATE: an inference call produces a complete task ticket, a failed call raises a trouble ticket, a call with no caller identity records 'unknown'. FEEDS BACK: a red names which field is missing or which integration failed.
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when every inference call via the domain produces a complete task ticket with caller, request, response, model/provider selection, and outcome, and failures raise trouble tickets. WRONG INTENT if the ticket is a parallel store, adds latency, or duplicates trouble infrastructure.
falsifier.horizon: Moderate — extends existing interceptor.py infrastructure with more fields + trouble integration.

questions.a: EXTENDS, NOT REPLACES: the-inference-ticket-comes-back-whole (PROVED) built the reader and raw response body. This adds caller identity, selection rationale, escalation history, and trouble integration to the same rows.
CALL CHAIN vs MESSAGE ENVELOPE: two mechanisms for caller identity. Call stack is implicit (fragile); envelope field is explicit (robust). Design fork for the chart chain.
TASK TICKET IS THE ROW: no separate artifact. The inference_calls row IS the task ticket. One store, extended.

how.extends_existing: Extend the inference_calls rows (interceptor.py) with new fields: caller identity, model/provider specified vs selected, escalation history, exceptions, graph tree nodes consulted, outcome.
how.caller_identity: Either Python call stack inspection or explicit envelope field on the request dict. Akien: 'call chain or message envelope.' Chart-chain question.
how.trouble_integration: On failure, domain.resolve calls TroubleDevice.raise with the inference call's canonical as identity. On existing trouble, the count increments (the damping pattern). On unresolvable failure, an intelligible error message is returned.
how.no_parallel_store: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-31. Was: 'The task ticket IS the extended inference_calls row.' Now: the inference call becomes a TASK the inference proxy performs, producing an ARTIFACT stored in .cairn (instance-space logging). The task ticket IS the return value — the receiver or their shim extracts the actual reply, making the call inspectable. The artifact is a single file, not a DB row.
how.return_value_design: The task ticket (artifact) becomes the return value of the inference call. The receiver or their shim extracts the actual reply from it. This makes every call inspectable — the receiver can choose to examine what happened, not just consume the answer.
how.storage: .cairn instance-space logging, not the inference_calls DB table. The DB table may still hold summary/index rows, but the full record is the artifact.

watchme.trigger: after the first 20 inference calls that carry the extended fields
watchme.enough: when at least 10 calls have non-null caller identity and at least 1 failure has triggered a trouble ticket, OR 100 calls with zero trouble integrations
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact: field population rate and trouble integration count
watchme.consumer: the trouble lane on a silent failure

decisions.text: WHERE THE BUILD STANDS (2026-09-17, CC; pre-approved through PROVEME). Five files carry the whole build, all under cairn/devices/inference_domain/: domain.py (the ticket itself), device.py (the caller rides the envelope), probes/are_inference_task_tickets_complete.py (NEW, the WATCHME probe), proofs/test_task_ticket.py (NEW, the proof) and three amended sibling proofs (test_an_inference_call_logs_that_it_started.py, test_inference_domain.py, test_resolve_verb.py). The 'how' field's 2026-08-31 supersession governs: the task ticket is NOT an extended inference_calls DB row and NOT a new store beside the cache — it is ONE JSON FILE PER CALL in instance-space under the domain's own address, and the call's return value names it. The cache table is untouched; the trail (the 'started'/'answered'/'refused' jsonl lines under logs/inference_domain/0) is untouched except that a refusal now lands one extra 'raise_trouble' line beside its 'refused' line. No proof reads the live instance: every proof isolates roots with domain.set_diagnostic_roots({**address.ROOTS, 'instance': scratch_dir(...)}) from cairn/devices/tester/scratch.py, so a proof run leaves nothing under the live tickets/ folder (measured: 39 leaked fixture tickets from the first draft were trashed and the leak closed before this line was written).

decisions.text: WHERE THE ARTIFACT LIVES AND WHAT IT IS NAMED. domain.tickets_dir(roots=None) returns address.instance_path('inference_domain', 0, roots or _trail._diagnostic_roots) / 'tickets' — live that is $HOME/.cairn/devices/inference_domain/0/tickets/ (instance-space, never git). The folder is created on the first write (mkdir parents=True, exist_ok=True). One file per resolve() call, named <YYYYmmddTHHMMSSffffff>-<canonical_digest[:12]>-<pid>-<per-process counter>.json, and the ticket's 'id' field IS that filename's stem, so a ticket can be found from its id and vice versa with no index. The full schema is domain._TICKET_FIELDS = ('id','caller','request','canonical','verdict','outcome','specified','selected','response','cost','timings','trouble') — every key present on every ticket (a hit, a miss and a refusal all write all twelve; absent values are None, never a missing key). 'canonical' is the canonicalized request and 'canonical_digest' rides beside it; 'cache' names the table the call went through; 'timings' is {'started','finished','elapsed_ms'} in UTC ISO stamps; 'verdict' is 'hit'|'miss'|'refused'. domain.read_task_tickets(roots=None, limit=None) lists them newest first (an unreadable file comes back as {'id', 'unreadable': <error>} rather than being skipped — Law 7). The write is plain Path.write_text of json.dumps(indent=2, sort_keys=True); measured cost of _write_task_ticket is under 50 ms in the proof and the whole cached resolve stays under 2 s, which is the falsifier's 'adds latency' clause held by a tooth rather than by a claim.
decisions.step: unlisted: WHERE THE ARTIFACT LIVES AND WHAT IT IS NAMED. domain.ticket

decisions.text: CALLER IDENTITY — BOTH MECHANISMS, IN THIS ORDER, AND 'unknown' IS A VALUE NOT A GAP. Akien's line 'call chain or message envelope' is settled as BOTH, tried in order: (1) DECLARED — over the bus, InferenceDomainDevice._handle_resolve reads envelope.get('sender') (the bus stamps sender on every envelope; nothing in the domain trusts a body field for it) and passes it as domain.resolve(request, ..., caller=<sender>); the ticket then carries caller={'identity': '<sender>', 'how': 'declared'}. (2) CALL_CHAIN — a direct Python call with caller=None walks inspect.stack() via domain._frame_identity(frames): it skips frames whose filename starts with '<' (stdin/exec pseudo-files), frames whose file does not exist, frames inside domain.py itself, and frames outside the repo root (address.ROOTS['repo']); the first surviving frame yields '<repo-relative path>:<function>' and the ticket carries how='call_chain'. (3) NONE — if neither yields anything (measured by the tooth calling caller_identity(None, frames=[])) the ticket carries {'identity': 'unknown', 'how': 'none'} — the string 'unknown' is what the falsifier's proves_green names, and the probe counts such a ticket as 'named' == False but NOT as incomplete (ticket_lacks only reds a missing or empty caller.identity). The function is domain.caller_identity(explicit=None, *, frames=None) and the seam is the keyword-only caller parameter added to resolve() and to the device's one call site; no other signature changed.
decisions.step: unlisted: CALLER IDENTITY — BOTH MECHANISMS, IN THIS ORDER, AND 'unkno

decisions.text: TROUBLE ON A FAILED CALL — THE MECHANISM THAT EXISTS, NOT ONE THAT WAS IMAGINED. There is no TroubleDevice.raise verb on the bus; the trouble lane's one door is DiagnosticBase.raise_trouble(identity, *, why, detail=None, now=None) at cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py:321, which every DiagnosticBase holder already inherits — it emits a 'raise_trouble' line into the raiser's own log home and pokes the trouble lane (_poke_trouble_lane), returning a record with keys 'pointer', 'home' and 'poke' (poke reads 'sent', or 'held for the beat — no notifier wired', or 'refused: ...'; it never raises except TroubleRaiseRefused on an empty identity/why). So domain.resolve, in its except branch after the trail's 'refused' emit, does: raiser = sink if hasattr(sink, 'raise_trouble') else _trail (the device's debug_sink when running under the device, the module _trail when called directly); record = raiser.raise_trouble(f'inference-refused-{canonical_digest[:16]}', why=<one line naming the refusal type and the domain>, detail={'refused': <exception class name>, 'detail': str(exc)[:2000], 'domain': ..., 'caller': ..., 'canonical_digest': ...}, now=moment). The identity IS the canonical digest as the how asked (prefixed so the lane can tell an inference refusal from any other pointer), which is what lets the lane's damping count a repeat of the same canonical instead of opening a second trouble. 'Failure' means any exception out of resolver(request) — RouteRefused, a transport error, an unreachable host, anything. The trouble is raised AFTER the ticket's fields are known and the ticket carries trouble={'identity': record['pointer'], 'poke': record['poke'], 'home': record['home']}; if raise_trouble itself throws, the ticket still writes with trouble={'identity': None, 'poke': 'unraised: <error>'} so the failure is loud in the record (Law 7) rather than lost. The exception is then RE-RAISED to a direct caller with refusal.task_ticket = <the ticket path> set on it; over the bus the device catches it and REPLIES {'outcome': 'refused', 'refused': <type>, 'detail': ..., 'ticket': <path>, 'model': ..., 'hit': False, 'answer': None} — the 'intelligible error message' the how asked for, with the ticket path the receiver can open. This is why the sibling proof test_an_inference_call_logs_that_it_started.py's refusal tooth was narrowed from 'exactly one line' to 'exactly one refused line, and every other line is raise_trouble': the second line is this ticket's design, carried by this decision, not plaster.
decisions.step: unlisted: TROUBLE ON A FAILED CALL — THE MECHANISM THAT EXISTS, NOT ON

decisions.text: SPECIFIED VERSUS SELECTED. domain._specified(request, domain_name) reads what the caller ASKED FOR off the request: {'model': request.get('model'), 'provider': request.get('provider'), 'domain': <the domain name the request resolved under>, 'kind': request.get('kind')}. domain._selected(provenance) reads what the route ACTUALLY CHOSE off the resolver's provenance dict, keeping whichever of 'model', 'provider', 'host', 'path', 'route_walked' are present (a hit copies the prior row's provenance so a cached answer still names the model that once produced it; a refusal writes selected={} because nothing was selected). The two are separate keys on the ticket ('specified', 'selected') precisely so that a disagreement is visible per call — the proof's tooth asks for model 'fixture-asked:1b' and has the resolver report 'fixture-served:7b', then asserts the ticket carries both and they differ. Escalation history and graph-tree nodes consulted (named in the original 'extends_existing' text) are NOT on the ticket: no route today records an escalation ladder or a tree walk on its provenance, so there is nothing to copy; when the route grows those fields _selected picks them up by name and this decision is the place that says so.

decisions.text: THE PROOF AND ITS PROVES BLOCK. cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_task_ticket.py, pytest-shaped, ends with the print_teeth_main runner. cairn.tools.proof_coverage.clauses(ticket) reads this ticket's falsifier as the single clause 'all' (no (1)(2) markers in proves_red), so PROVES = {'ea4a6151300f': {'all': 'test_every_inference_call_produces_a_complete_task_ticket'}} — ONE composite tooth that runs the seven narrow teeth end to end (each narrow tooth still prints on its own so a red names which half fell). The seven: one call writes one ticket naming the canonical and every _TICKET_FIELDS key; the caller rides the envelope through the real InferenceDomainDevice (instantiated via __new__ with host.ollama_resolver monkeypatched and domain.resolve wrapped to pin the fixture cache table) and lands as how='declared'; a direct call is named off the call chain and caller_identity(None, frames=[]) yields 'unknown'; specified and selected disagree and both are recorded; a refusing resolver raises the trouble (the trail carries a raise_trouble line naming the identity, the exception class and the digest), the direct call re-raises with task_ticket set, and the device shim returns a refused reply carrying the ticket path; the ticket is not a parallel store (a second identical call is served from the cache with verdict 'hit', _write_task_ticket runs under 50 ms, the cached resolve under 2 s); and the probe shares the same predicate (domain.ticket_lacks) and fires on a fixture set that lacks fields. Fixtures use a nonce-named cache table _probe_task_ticket_<nonce> dropped at cleanup along with its registry row, and every tooth runs under isolated roots via scratch_dir. Green twice: 8/8 (seven narrow + the composite). Sealed under the tester before PROVEME; proof_coverage.lacks(ticket) == [] is checked after the forward BUILDME crossing names this proof as proven_by (the 2026-09-06 and 2026-09-07 crossings named test_an_inference_call_logs_that_it_started.py and test_proof_coverage.py, which declare nothing for this ticket — the ticket was kicked back to TICKETME on 2026-09-17 exactly so the forward crossing could carry the right proof).

decisions.text: THE WATCHME PROBE. cairn/devices/inference_domain/probes/are_inference_task_tickets_complete.py declares module-level PROBE = Probe(why=..., trigger=_trigger, to='harbor_master', body={'nexus': 'hypothesize', 'kind': 'efficacy'}, carry=_carry, enough=_enough, horizon=1000), berthed at exactly the path the ticket's watchme.probe names so the WATCHME emission gate resolves ARMED. It reads domain.read_task_tickets() (the live folder, read-only) and judges each with domain.ticket_lacks — the same predicate the proof uses, so the probe and the proof cannot disagree about what 'complete' means. judge_tickets returns {tickets, incomplete: [{id, lacks}], named (caller.identity not 'unknown'), refused, troubled (trouble.identity set)}. _trigger fires once at least 20 tickets exist and any is incomplete (the ticket's 'after the first 20 inference calls'); _enough is the ticket's own sentence made a predicate: no incomplete AND ((named >= 10 and troubled >= 1) OR (tickets >= 100 and troubled == 0)); _carry deposits field_population_rate, trouble_integrations, the counts, the first 50 incomplete ids with their lacks, the owning ticket id, against_falsifier and suggests. Smoke-fired once over the live folder: 0 tickets at the time, no trigger. The probe carries no authority (Law 6): it deposits and pokes harbor_master; re-opening the ticket is the owner's act.

WHAT THIS BUILD DOES NOT DO, SO THE READER STOPS LOOKING FOR IT. It does not touch cairn/devices/trouble/ (the lane is reached through the inherited raise_trouble door, which is the dependency the ticket named); it does not add rows or columns to the inference_calls table or any other table (the 'storage' clause: instance-space files, not the DB); it does not change the shape of a successful reply beyond adding the 'ticket' key (path string) — the answer is still 'answer', so existing receivers keep working and a receiver that wants the whole record opens the file (the 'return_value_design' clause satisfied by pointer rather than by inlining the artifact into every reply, because the artifact includes the raw response body and inlining it would double every bus message); and it does not wait on state-machine-physics (the dependency list's fourth line) — the inference call's lifecycle is recorded by the ticket's verdict/outcome/timings fields, and nothing here rides the transition table, so that BUILDME ticket is not a hold on this one.

decisions.text: THE THREE SIBLING AMENDMENTS, ONE EACH, NOTHING INFERRED. (a) proofs/test_an_inference_call_logs_that_it_started.py — the refusal tooth used to assert the trail held exactly ONE record for a refused ask; it now reads refused = [r for r in records if r['gate'] == 'refused']; assert len(refused) == 1; and asserts every other record's gate is 'raise_trouble' (with a comment citing ea4a6151300f) — the second line is the trouble raise this ticket adds, so the tooth was narrowed to what it actually measured (one refusal line) rather than to a count that the design changed. (b) proofs/test_inference_domain.py — no tooth text changed; its _main now wraps the whole run in domain.set_diagnostic_roots({**_address.ROOTS, 'instance': scratch_dir('cairn_infer_proof_')}) with a finally that restores set_diagnostic_roots(None), and the one tooth that already set its own roots (the both-records tooth) saves outer = getattr(domain._trail, '_diagnostic_roots', None) and restores it — because this proof calls resolve() 32 times and, before the change, wrote 32 task tickets and four raise_trouble emissions into the LIVE instance folder and log home (measured; the leaked tickets were trashed and the four fixture-born troubles cleared with the reason in what_changed). (c) proofs/test_resolve_verb.py — same shape, no tooth text changed: its __main__ sets isolated roots via scratch_dir('cairn_resolve_verb_') and restores None in a finally (it wrote 7 live tickets before). All three print GREEN twice after the change and were resealed under the tester (validations beside them carry the new fingerprints).

THE PROOF'S SEAMS, SPELLED. host.ollama_resolver comes from cairn/devices/inference_domain/host.py (the device's own module; device.py imports it as host and calls host.ollama_resolver(model=model, temperature=temperature) inside _handle_resolve) — the bus tooth monkeypatches host.ollama_resolver = lambda **kw: <fixture resolver> for the duration of the tooth and restores it in a finally, so the real _handle_resolve runs with no host dialled. domain.ticket_lacks(ticket: dict) -> list[str] lives in domain.py directly under read_task_tickets and returns [] for a complete ticket, else the names of what is missing, in this order: every key of _TICKET_FIELDS absent from the dict (by field name); 'caller.identity' when caller has no truthy identity; 'outcome.kind' when outcome.kind is not one of 'answered'|'refused'; for a refused outcome, 'outcome.refused' when the exception class name is absent and 'trouble' when the trouble block is falsy; and 'timings.started' / 'timings.finished' / 'timings.elapsed_ms' for each missing timing. It is the ONE predicate: the proof's composite tooth asserts ticket_lacks(t) == [] over every ticket it writes, and the probe judges the live folder with the same function, so the two cannot disagree about the word 'complete'.

judge_tickets, SPELLED. In probes/are_inference_task_tickets_complete.py: def judge_tickets(tickets: list[dict]) -> dict imports ticket_lacks from cairn.devices.inference_domain.domain and walks the list once: a ticket carrying 'unreadable' (read_task_tickets' shape for a file that would not parse) is counted incomplete with lacks == [<the error text>]; otherwise lacks = ticket_lacks(t) and a non-empty result appends {'id': t['id'], 'lacks': lacks} to incomplete; named counts tickets whose caller.identity is set and not 'unknown'; refused counts outcome.kind == 'refused'; troubled counts tickets whose trouble.identity is set. It returns {'tickets': len(tickets), 'incomplete': [...], 'named': n, 'refused': n, 'troubled': n}. survey_the_tickets() is judge_tickets(read_task_tickets()) and is the read the probe's _trigger/_enough/_carry share; the proof's probe tooth feeds judge_tickets a fixture list (one complete ticket, one stripped of caller and timings) and asserts the stripped one is listed with those lacks, so the probe's judgement is proved without touching the live folder. ONE LATE ADDITION, made after D1-D8 were written and carried here so the record is whole: the chart's fourth criterion asks that the trouble NAME the ticket path, so domain._ticket_path(ticket, roots=None) now allocates the filename BEFORE the trouble is raised (the counter/stamp/digest/pid name, no write), the raise_trouble detail carries 'ticket': str(path), and _close(..., path=ticket_path) writes to that pre-allocated path; the refusal tooth asserts err.task_ticket appears in the raise_trouble emission. Live-fired once: the forced failure's trouble folded into CairnCommons/troubles/inference-refused-f40cd8b68f88d908.json with the ticket path in its occurrence detail.

CANONICALIZATION IS REUSED, NOT REBUILT. The ticket's 'canonical' is domain.canonicalize(request) (domain.py line 348), which already existed for the cache and is the same string the cache row keys on: view = {k: v for k, v in request.items() if k != 'domain'}; json.dumps(view, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False) — the domain NAME is excluded, the dressing content (the system text the domain applied) stays in. 'canonical_digest' is domain.canonical_digest(canonical) (line 367): hashlib.sha256(text.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest() — the FULL 64-hex digest is stored on the ticket; only the FILENAME and the trouble identity take prefixes of it ([:12] in the filename, [:16] in 'inference-refused-<...>'). The proof asserts ticket['canonical'] == domain.canonicalize(request) on a ticket the fixture wrote, so the reuse is measured rather than assumed.

SETTLES _write_task_ticket vs _close (MEASURED 2026-09-24, cairn/devices/inference_domain/domain.py): they are two functions with distinct roles, not one. _write_task_ticket(ticket, *, roots=None, path=None) -> Path (line 298) is the module-level writer: one JSON file per call, loud on failure, allocating its own path via _ticket_path unless handed one. _close(verdict, *, outcome, selected, response, cost, trouble, path=None) -> Path | None (line 491) is a closure nested inside the call path: it stamps verdict/outcome/selected/response/cost/trouble/timings onto the ticket, then calls _write_task_ticket(ticket, path=path) (line 507) inside its own try, so an unwritable ticket is said on stderr and the answer still reaches the caller. 'Pre-allocate then _close(..., path=ticket_path)' means: _ticket_path allocates, _close stamps and delegates the write to _write_task_ticket at that path.
